positioning: A general’s confidence in a teacup of fluff.
story: The Pomeranian is the size of a teapot and has the confidence of a general. It marches into any room, fluffs itself to full height, and expects applause.

The surprise is its ancestry. The Pomeranian descends from large Spitz dogs of Pomerania, a Baltic region of Europe, that herded sheep and pulled sleds. Those dogs weighed up to thirty pounds. Over generations, breeders shrank them to fit in a lap.

Royalty did the rest. Queen Charlotte brought Pomeranians to Britain in the 1700s. Queen Victoria fell for the breed in 1888, when she acquired a small one in Florence, and she bred them smaller still. Fashion followed the Queen.
Fame found small dogs in odd places. Two of the three dogs that survived the Titanic were Pomeranians.

The attitude has never shrunk. A Pomeranian barks at mail carriers, nods at snowflakes, and guards the sofa from anything larger than a cushion. The fluff is real. Under the double coat, the dog is mostly confidence.
Brush it often and handle it gently. In return you get a loyal shadow who thinks you are the most important person in the house, and is usually right.
rank_cap: A fox-faced fluffball with a general’s confidence (AKC)
fblocks: Named for Pomerania, the Baltic region now split between Poland and Germany.
Marco, the Pomeranian Queen Victoria brought home from Florence in 1888. Two Pomeranians that survived the sinking of the Titanic.
Barks readily and needs early training. Daily brushing keeps the double coat tidy. Small bones, so handle gently. Dental care matters.
A thick double coat, most often orange, but also red, cream, black, sable, and more. A plume tail lies over the back.
Three to seven pounds, though its ancestors reached thirty. Recognized by the AKC in 1900.
days: The Pomeranian has claimed the best chair. No appeal is possible.
Pomeranians descend from Spitz dogs many times their size.
Queen Victoria fell for Pomeranians in 1888 and bred them smaller.
Confidence is not a matter of size. Ask any Pomeranian.
A Pomeranian will bark at one snowflake and call it victory.
Two of the three dogs saved from the Titanic were Pomeranians.
Two Pomeranians on a cushion make one warm, fluffy cloud.
last_walk:
The tiny sweater is on, and the leash is ready.
A Pomeranian does not think it is small. It thinks the whole world has been scaled down for its convenience. It steps to the door, chin up, tail high, and waits for you to catch up. The door opens, and the snowy yard is ready to roam.
